Qualitative findings further revealed a tension between empathy-oriented outputs and users' desire to express legitimate anger or direct disagreement. We contribute exploratory design guidance for treating AI-assisted counterspeech as deliberative co-writing rather than automated text production.
label: cs.SI

description: Sum-rank analogues of Reed--Muller codes over Abelian Galois extensions. Let $\mathbb L/\mathbb K$ be a finite Abelian Galois extension with a fixed decomposition $\mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb L/\mathbb K)=\langleσ_1\rangle\times\cdots\times\langleσ_m\rangle$. We show that the quotient of the multivariate skew polynomial ring $\mathbb L[x_1,\ldots,x_m;σ_1,\ldots,σ_m]$ by suitable central polynomials $H_1(x_1),\ldots,H_m(x_m)$ is isomorphic to a product of $t$ copies of $\mathrm{End}_{\mathbb K}(\mathbb L)$, so that one skew polynomial represents all blocks of a sum-rank metric space. The sum-rank weight of an element equals the rank of an associated Dickson matrix and of a generalized Moore matrix. Using this, we define sum-rank Reed--Muller-type codes and show that their dimension and minimum distance are given by the formulas for affine Cartesian codes with side lengths $\mathrm{deg}\,H_1,\ldots,\mathrm{deg}\,H_m$; the same holds for codes supported on lower sets. The family contains as special cases linearized Reed--Solomon codes, Gabidulin codes, rank-metric Reed--Muller codes, and affine Cartesian codes. Over finite fields, every linearized Reed--Muller code of Berardini and Caruso is, after a monomial change of variables, a monomial code in our framework. This gives the dimension of all these codes, and their exact minimum distance in every degree whenever the support is a lower set.
label: cs.IT

description: Gradient Discrete Schrodinger Bridge Matching for Peptide Generation. The optimal control of a discrete Schrödinger bridge is a discrete gradient, a difference of vertex potentials, but recent models such as MadSBM instead learn a free control on the edges by cross-entropy. We prove that this leaves the action uncontrolled: cross-entropy identifies the control only up to a state-dependent shift (a gauge), and the action is $\operatorname{KL}(r\|p)$ plus a gauge term the loss never constrains. We propose GDSBM, which writes the control as a difference of vertex potentials and adds the action to the loss; pinning the gauge costs no expressiveness and makes the action a property of the model, so the penalty acts on the model and not on the gauge. On peptide generation our MadSBM reimplementation has a free-gauge action of order $10^{8}$ for a gauge-fixed value of $6.5$, against $1.5$ for GDSBM, with no quality loss that three seeds can detect. The gradient form also fits guidance, which becomes the addition of a potential: guided toward a net charge of $+3$ at pH~7, GDSBM is closer than MadSBM, over three seeds, to its exact tempered target in total variation at every guidance strength (at $β=1$, $81\%$ of samples in the target window against $74\%$, for a target of $97\%$); we claim no statistical significance.
label: math.OC

description: A Sharp Analysis of Fixed Offset Hash Tables. We consider the class of open addressing hash tables that uses a fixed offset sequence $r_0,r_1,\ldots,r_{n-1}$ to find an open slot in the table. As special cases this subsumes linear probing ($r_i=i$) and quadratic probing ($r_i=i^2$). We give a simple analysis that the expected insertion time when the load factor is $1-ε$ is $O(ε^{-2})$. This bound is tight for linear probing (but not for quadratic probing), so the analysis cannot be improved at this level of generality.
label: cs.DS

description: A second-order linear decoupled scheme with a relaxed zero-energy variable for Rayleigh-Bénard convection. We construct a second-order, linear, and fully decoupled scheme for Rayleigh--Bénard convection between Navier-slip walls. The nonlinear terms are treated explicitly and multiplied by a scalar with exact value $1$ and no energy contributed to the continuous problem. As a result, each BDF2 step, with a rotational pressure correction, solves only constant-coefficient linear problems. For the time discretization, we prove that, for any time-step, the energy decays when the walls have equal temperatures, under a condition on the thermal weight, and the energy is bounded on finite time intervals when heated from below. Relaxing the scalar towards $1$ preserves both estimates. Energy stability does not control the accuracy of the scalar; the velocity and temperature fields are computed with its unrelaxed value, whose deviation from $1$ scales like $(E/C)(δt/τ)^3$ for kinetic energy $E$, time-scale $τ$ of the flow, and weight $C$ of the scalar equation. In our tests, choosing $C$ comparable to $E$ keeps this deviation small and doubles the largest time-step for which steady rolls are reproduced to a relative difference of $10^{-8}$. With Taylor--Hood elements, we observe second-order convergence in time, recover the critical Rayleigh numbers, and match published Nusselt numbers to within $0.5\%$. A three-dimensional implementation passes corresponding validation tests.
label: physics.flu-dyn

description: AfterDeleteBench: Auditing Post-Deletion Information Persistence in LLM Agents. Many LLM agents maintain external persistent memory and derive additional state from past interactions, such as summaries. Deleting an original memory record therefore need not remove information carried by its descendants. We introduce AfterDeleteBench, a controlled behavioral audit for this failure mode in fixed-weight LLM agents. For each synthetic secret, we compare an exposed-then-deleted agent with an otherwise matched agent that was never exposed to the secret, allowing post-deletion recovery to be attributed to the original exposure. In our primary setting, a single query recovers the deleted secret from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct in roughly two thirds of cases, while matched never-exposed controls have zero recovery. Crucially, recovery does not require a surviving verbatim copy: when the complete secret string is absent and only separately stored components remain under a public composition rule, exact reconstruction succeeds in 62-99% of cases across Qwen, Mistral, and Phi-3. We also show that the response interface is part of the measurement system: target-bearing replies can be scored as failures when the requested format and parser are misaligned. Finally, we separate reconstruction from write-back and fresh-session recall. Provenance-aware closure eliminates observed recovery in the tested positive-baseline settings, whereas an exact-literal write filter blocks reinsertion but cannot erase information already present. Together, these results show that source deletion should be evaluated behaviorally at the level of the agent and its memory system, not only as a storage operation.
label: cs.CR

description: Synthetic 2D magnetic turbulence with controlled island structuring. Magnetic turbulence remains up to this day not fully understood, despite its important role in the behavior of plasmas. A recurring ingredient in plasma turbulence is the spontaneous formation and evolution of plasmoids. These represent magnetic islands on current sheets in two-dimensional turbulent magnetic fields that are consistently found in high-resolution direct numerical simulations (DNSs) using a magnetohydrodynamic description. However, such simulations require considerable amounts of computational power. Synthetic turbulence models provide an alternative, cheap approach to the generation of fully-developed turbulent fields. In this work, we first present an extension of our open-source, general synthetic turbulence BxC toolkit that is specifically tailored to generate 2D turbulent magnetic fields. We then use a novel physically motivated, but purely geometric construction that generates current sheet island chains, which results in fields that visually match the ones obtained through DNSs. We show how this construction affects the magnetic field lines and find a correlation with the formation of magnetic O-points and X-points. The magnetic flux and size of the islands in the field are found to match well with theoretical scaling laws. Lastly, we show BxC's capabilities by generating a 2D $N\times N$ turbulent magnetic field of resolution $N = 100000$, going beyond the state-of-the-art reached by simulations, on a single CPU with modest computational resources. Our construction maintains direct control over the inertial range, and allows to make morphological changes to the plasmoids and fields, demonstrating plasmoid appearance, disappearance and merging.
label: physics.plasm-ph

description: RIDDLE: Revealing Irregularities through Distributional Discrepancies in Latent-space via Stein-Witness Estimation. RIDDLE is a new method for resonant anomaly detection that uses a scalar Stein-witness function to identify discrepancies between unlabeled signal-region events and a background distribution inferred from dijet-mass sidebands. The witness is optimized in a latent representation of auxiliary jet observables against a differentiable background reference, without requiring an explicit signal model. The method is evaluated using simulated LHC Olympics dijet events and compared with idealized and supervised benchmarks that share the same statistical construction but have access to additional signal or background information. RIDDLE demonstrates strong signal--background discrimination comparable to the idealized benchmark, while largely preserving the background dijet-mass spectrum under anomaly-score selection. Tests incorporating additional angular information and deliberately mass-correlated features further demonstrate the method's robustness under the studied conditions. Together, these results highlight the potential of RIDDLE as a robust, data-driven approach for enhanced resonance searches that combines effective anomaly discrimination with background-shape preservation.
label: hep-ph

description: Stochastic Geometry Analysis and Optimization for Multi-LEO Satellite-Assisted Communications. Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites are vital in providing seamless connectivities to ground users (GUs). However, complex satellite-to-ground propagation and non-negligible satellite failure probabilities make single-satellite transmission unreliable. To address this issue, we consider a multi-LEO-satellite communication network (mLEO-CN), where a typical GU is served by multiple LEO satellites. The satellite locations are modeled as a binomial point process on a sphere and ordered according to their distances to the GU. To improve communication reliability, a serial communication scheme is adopted, in which the subsequent satellite is activated only when all preceding satellites fail to satisfy the target signal-to-noise ratio threshold. By employing the tool of stochastic geometry, we derive key performance metrics, including overall transmission success probability, average transmission rate, and end-to-end delay under the serial communication scheme by incorporating both shadowed Rician (SR) fading and satellite failure probabilities. To improve analytical tractability, we derive asymptotic expressions for the end-to-end transmission success probability in two special cases by leveraging the asymptotic expression of the SR fading model and a Gamma-distribution, and further propose a cluster-based approximation approach for the overall transmission success probability. Building on these analyses, we formulate an optimization problem to maximize the ratio of the overall transmission success probability to the end-to-end delay, and obtain its solution using a one-dimensional search approach. Numerical results validate the analysis, reveal the impact of key parameters, and identify the optimal number of serving LEO satellites under different constellation altitudes.
label: eess.SP

description: The Penrose Correspondence over a Non-Archimedean Field. Let $K$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic different from $2$ and let $V$ be a four-dimensional symplectic $K$-vector space. We study the Penrose incidence correspondence $\mathbb{P}(V) \leftarrow \mathrm{Flag}(1,2;V) \rightarrow \mathrm{Gr}(2,V)$ after Berkovich analytification. The Klein quadric $\mathrm{Gr}(2,V)$ decomposes into the open orbit $\mathrm{Spin}(5)/\mathrm{Spin}(4)$ and the Lagrangian quadric, which parametrize respectively the projective lines transverse and tangent to the standard contact distribution on $\mathbb{P}(V)$. We construct explicit free discrete subgroups $Γ\subset\mathrm{PSp}(V)$ and analytic domains, cut out by Drinfeld upper half-spaces, in all three members of the incidence diagram. Both incidence projections are surjective on these domains, the three $Γ$-actions are free and properly discontinuous, and the Penrose double correspondence descends to the analytic quotients. The quotient of the twistor domain is a contact analytic threefold, and the Grassmannian domain is contained in the analytification of the $\mathrm{Spin}(5)/\mathrm{Spin}(4)$ open orbit.
label: math.AG

description: Pipelining vs. Combining in Aggregation Tasks. We study the aggregation task (convergecast) in networks in the case that the values to be aggregated do not fit in a single message. We assume that every node starts with an input value, and there is an aggregation operator that is commutative, associative, and length-preserving, i.e., the result of aggregating two values has the same length as each of the input values. Since values do not fit in a message, they are transferred in a ``train'' of pipelined messages, which must be terminated whenever we want to aggregate values. The goal is to minimize the makespan time of aggregating all values. We present general lower bounds on the problem and optimal algorithms for several prevalent parallel computing architectures, including the hypercube and complete bipartite graphs, under both the splittable and unsplittable flows models. We also present an $O(\log n)$ approximation for general graphs in the unsplittable flows model.
label: cs.DC

description: Auditing the Hand-Written Inputs of Learned Access Control. Learned access control is typically deployed behind two hand-built artefacts: a hard-deny set enforced by a small trusted shield, and a region map that decides which requests mined rules answer and which the learner answers. Verifying the shield or measuring the learner validates neither. We audit both on the five public ABAC Lab policies. First, we formalise hard-deny soundness and check it exhaustively over relations of up to 794,250 tuples. Clauses that faithfully transcribe an explicit restriction are unsound at rates of 0.50-0.70 across four elicitors - an author and three blind language-model elicitors - because prose scopes restrictions to a section while the grant relation is a disjunction over all rules: 97% of counterexamples are granted by other rules. Shipped unchecked, these deny sets would withhold 16-78% of everything the policies grant; certified, they withhold nothing. Vacuity, a second silent failure, also occurs. Second, hybrid routing needs a two-class, abstaining rule set that ABAC miners do not emit, and ranking a mixed-effect candidate pool under a cap is one-class in all 24 cells for the two commonest ranking keys. Third, for additive losses the hybrid-versus-learner effect factorises into covered mass times a rule-learner risk contrast that must be reported on both false-non-grant and false-permit loss: on two real policies, most selection rules give opposite verdicts on the two losses, and the one favourable on both holds for one policy, one learner configuration and a band of noise levels. A released artefact regenerates and checks every reported number.
label: cs.CR

description: Orbital-coherence memory in electrical transport and its self-consistent Maxwell response. An internal electronic coherence changes electrical transport only when it feeds back on the physical current. We develop a reduced description of this feedback and distinguish its exact consequences from the assumptions required for a microscopic realization. An opposite-parity two-orbital Hamiltonian identifies a current-coupled orbital force. Under an explicitly stated moment closure and collision ansatz, it yields a passive three-state response with an exponentially damped oscillatory memory. The resulting conductivity redistributes a fixed optical weight and predicts a nonmonotonic dependence of dc conduction on coherence damping at fixed remaining parameters. The orbital reduction constrains the coupling and internal frequency through a shared bare splitting, providing a test beyond unconstrained spectral fitting. A charge-conserving spatial extension couples to Maxwell equations through a positive energy balance and separates the constitutive response from longitudinal collective and transverse electromagnetic modes. We formulate complex-conductivity and transmission tests, including the limits of parameter identification over a finite bandwidth. The model supplies a conditional connection between orbital dynamics, transport memory, and electromagnetic observables; conductivity alone does not establish a uniquely quantum mechanism, and a material-specific collision calculation and closure-error assessment remain necessary.
label: physics.app-ph

description: $N \to Δ$ Transition Form Factors in the Thermal AdS/QCD Soft-Wall Model with Modified Propagators. We investigate electromagnetic (EM) and axial vector (AV) form factors of the nucleon-Delta baryon transition within the thermal AdS/QCD soft-wall model. While the vector bulk-to-boundary propagator admits a well-behaved analytical solution, the transverse axial vector equation of motion involves the vacuum expectation value of the bifundamental scalar (generating chiral symmetry breaking). Due to this, the axial propagator diverges asymptotically, rendering it unsuitable for computing observables in the soft-wall model. To address this problem, we implement a regularization for the axial propagator in the form of a momentum-dependent cut-off, that identifies its correct physical regime. This is achieved via an interior constraint approach to the boundary-value problem, that determines the cut-off point. The consistency of this procedure is verified near the UV limit. As a proof of concept, we test this modified propagator (and also a parametrically deformed version of it) to estimate axial vector form factors of the $N \to Δ$ transition, and find results moderately comparable with form factor profiles from experimental observations, lattice QCD, and other theoretical models. Equipped with this regularization, the thermal soft-wall model becomes a useful tool to probe thermal characteristics of QCD form factors. We demonstrate this for both, the EM and AV sectors of the $N \to Δ$ transition.
label: hep-ph

description: Predictive electronic feedback control for narrow-linewidth lasers. Narrow-linewidth lasers are essential for various key atom-laser interaction processes and optical setups in quantum coherent control, quantum precision measurement, and quantum information science. The Pound-Drever-Hall (PDH) technique is the standard method for the frequency-stabilization of narrow-linewidth lasers, but the inherent time delay in its feedback loop inevitably induces excessive phase noise, commonly known as servo bumps. Previous solutions primarily rely on additional optical components outside the electronic feedback control loop. Here, we propose and implement a generic method based on the Smith predictor to address the time-delay issue entirely within the electronic part of the PDH feedback control loop. We systematically demonstrate its capability to suppress phase noise and reduce servo bumps by adding only a single Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) controller to the loop. This class of methods is demonstrated to be conceptually concise with minimal hardware overhead, effective in practice, and holds potential for a wide variety of future applications.
label: physics.optics

description: Control, stability, and stabilization of some classes of linear time-delay systems. This monograph presents a selection of the author's recent works on the control, stability, and stabilization of some classes of linear time-delay systems. After a detailed introduction to topics related to time-delay systems covered in the monograph, its main contents are presented in a series of mostly independent chapters.
label: math.OC

description: An asymptotic $Γ$-BMT inequality. We refine a bound of Cheng-Feyzbakhsh to prove an asymptotic $Γ$-Bayer-Macrì-Toda ($Γ$-BMT) inequality on every smooth polarized complex threefold. The proof relies on a reduction to small tilt stability parameters. Using this inequality we verify Feyzbakhsh-Thomas's condition $(wBG)$ whenever $K_{X}$ is numerically proportional to the polarization. For polarized Calabi-Yau threefolds, this yields a reduction of positive rank generalized Donaldson-Thomas (DT) invariants to those counting sheaves pure in codimension one. We further express these invariants in terms of rank one generalized DT invariants. Thus, the rank reductions of Feyzbakhsh-Thomas hold without assuming the BMT conjecture.
label: math.AG

description: Landau-Siegel zeros over a base field and effective Brauer-Siegel. Let k be a number field. We prove that for every quadratic extension F/k, every real zero beta of L(s, chi_{F/k}) satisfies (1 - beta) log d_F >= c(k) with an effective constant c(k) > 0, and we deduce (through a reduction of Stark) that the Brauer-Siegel theorem holds effectively and uniformly over all Galois extensions K of k, in the form h_K R_K >= c(k) d_K^{1/2} / ((2 pi)^{[K:Q]} log d_K). Stark's effective cases of the Brauer-Siegel theorem were the fields without quadratic subfields, since the quadratic subfields carried the ineffectivity of Siegel's theorem; over a base field k, the first result removes it. Both rely on a uniform bound for Chebotarev sums. Let K/k be a Galois extension with group G, and suppose S is a subset of G containing the identity. For any prime p of k, let delta_p be the proportion of the primes of K above p whose Frobenius lies in S. Then the sum over Np = d_K^C with C depending only on epsilon and the degree [K:Q]. The proof is Kerr's form of the OpenAI argument, simple vanishing at the points (iota theta)_{iota in S}, with theta in a box in O_K, and Masser's zero estimate. The field enters only through Masser's invariant of the lattice of points, which we compute to be [K:Q]/|S| by averaging over the Galois group of the normal closure. Over Q, the determinant method of Green, Barreto, and Kominers gives sharper Chebotarev bounds, and we explain the comparison.
label: math.NT

description: Benign cubic and quartic forms on the sphere. One considers the NP-hard problem of minimizing real cubic and quartic forms on the Euclidean unit sphere. One first extends the Hessian spectral characterization of local minima by the author. In particular one provides a gap-depth characterization of negative global and spurious minima, and proves that the minimum value of an odd degree-d form is recovered (up to the factor d(d -1)) by minimizing the smallest eigenvalue of its ambient Hessian over the sphere (and equivalently the unit ball). Next, one exhibits several classes of benign families of cubic and quartic forms (i.e. with no spurious local minima on the sphere) and prove that some are robust to small coefficient perturbation (i.e. the resulting form remains benign even if it leaves the initial family). Therefore the class of benign cubic and quartic forms is full-dimensional (in the ambient space of coefficients), for n $\ge$ 2. Also for every odd degree d, the class of benign degree-d forms increases with the dimension (however it does not imply that such forms become more frequent when the dimension increases).
label: math.OC

description: AgentPhishing: A Benchmark of LLM Email Agents Under Adaptive Attack. Computer-use agents increasingly handle private information and act on users' behalf across desktop and web applications, including email. Phishing therefore poses privacy and security risks that depend not only on whether agents recognize malicious messages, but also on how they respond. Existing phishing datasets were developed primarily for conventional detection, leaving agent susceptibility to persuasive malicious requests insufficiently characterized. To expose vulnerabilities that pre-existing datasets may miss, we introduce AgentPhishing, a benchmark for evaluating whether persuasive phishing attacks can evade detection and induce LLM email agents to comply with malicious requests. We develop PhishOpt, which optimizes reusable email-generation skills against individual agents under fixed benchmark constraints and a realism constraint. We analyze the generated emails using Cialdini's persuasion principles to identify strategies associated with agent failures and use these findings to construct a universal generation skill. Our evaluation shows that agents can handle pre-existing phishing emails safely yet remain susceptible to attacks adapted to agent behavior, while in an AgentPhishing evaluation of nine agents, four exhibit phishing-detection rates below $10\%$ and malicious-request compliance rates above $45\%$. These results highlight the limits of inferring agent safety from conventional phishing evaluations and the need to assess how agents respond to persuasive malicious requests.
label: cs.CR

description: Anisotropic spin hydrodynamics in a magnetized medium: entropy-current formulation and minimal linear modes. We formulate anisotropic relativistic spin hydrodynamics in a parity-even magnetized medium using an Israel--Stewart entropy-current construction. Treating the magnetic field at leading order in the gradient expansion reduces the rotational symmetry to $SO(2)$ and separates spin susceptibilities and dissipative transport into longitudinal, transverse, and mixed channels. A restricted quadratic entropy current yields transient equations for the retained dissipative stresses and spin fluxes. We analyze a minimal linear closure around an unpolarized homogeneous equilibrium, retaining dynamical magnetic-flux perturbations but no explicit spin-magnetization coupling; spin and magnetic fluctuations mix through the fluid variables. Infrared coefficient equations and ultraviolet characteristic expansions organize the magnetosonic and Alfvén-like spectra together with spectator spin-flux poles. The first-order truncation exhibits unstable boost-sector poles and superlinear large-wave-number branches, interpreted as diagnostics of the truncated equations rather than microscopic dispersion predictions. For the baseline parameters, finite relaxation times yield asymptotically linear propagation branches and finite relaxation poles, with no growing modes found on the sampled grid. The characteristic speeds depend nonmonotonically on spin transport and provide necessary light-cone diagnostics, without establishing general stability or strong hyperbolicity.
label: nucl-th

description: The center is the formal internal automorphism group. We prove that the deformation functor associated to an algebra over a sufficiently nice Koszul operad can be lifted to an operadic formal moduli problem over the Koszul dual operad. We further show that this operadic formal moduli problem corresponds to the derived center of the algebra under the operadic Lurie-Pridham correspondence. As an application, we prove that the classical Gerstenhaber algebra structure on polyvector fields of a commutative algebra agrees with the derived center of the algebra as an abelian Poisson algebra.
label: math.AT

description: The Spectral Edge at Large Central Charge and Black Hole Statistics. We introduce a new approach to high-energy spectra in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$, addressing the open challenge of incorporating spectral statistics into the modular bootstrap. Using the analytic theory of $L$-functions attached to two-dimensional CFTs, we leverage modular constraints among high-energy states to derive a sum rule relating the spectral edge to bulk spectral fluctuations. As an application, we establish a refined modular bootstrap bound: letting $Δ_1$ be the conformal dimension of the lightest excited Virasoro primary of a unitary CFT of central charge $c$, we show that $Δ_1 - {c-1\over 12} \leq o(c)$, with at most one exceptional value of the scalar gap at each sufficiently large $c$; moreover, along any sequence in $c$ for which such exceptional gaps are realized, the remaining gaps obey the stronger bound $Δ_1 - {c-1\over 12} \leq O(1)$. The result applies to theories with logarithmic rigidity of spectral counting fluctuations, as in random matrix theory.
label: hep-th

description: A Catalog of Spectral Properties for DESI DR1 Quasars. The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) is carrying out a five-year spectroscopic survey designed to map the large-scale structure of the Universe and obtain spectra for millions of galaxies and quasars over a wide redshift range. We present a value-added catalog of spectral properties for 1,717,774 unique quasars (1,774,723 spectra) in the DESI Data Release 1. We perform a uniform spectral decomposition of the quasar continuum, host galaxy emission (at $z 1$ where the pipeline redshift is heavily constrained by blueshifted high-ionization lines. We also provide local fits to several optical coronal lines, including \NeV~$\lambda3426$, [\ion{Fe}{7}]~$\lambda5722$, [\ion{Fe}{7}]~$\lambda6088$, and [\ion{Fe}{11}]~$\lambda7893$. We show that several emission-line ratios, including those involving coronal lines, vary systematically with Eddington ratio. The catalog is intended as a community resource for studies of quasar demographics, black hole accretion, emission-line physics, and the connection between the broad-, coronal-, and narrow-line regions.
label: astro-ph.GA

description: Tandem jets in crossflow: the enclosed-recirculation momentum exchange and the unsteady shear-layer dynamics. Twin tandem jets in crossflow are examined by 40\ kHz time-resolved particle image velocimetry (PIV) over nine spacing--velocity-ratio conditions ($L=2d$--$4d$, $r\approx3$--7; 68 twin cases, 11 single-jet records). The front jet is diluted: its trajectory lies below the single-jet reference, with a near-field segment up to 40\% shorter, and its velocity ratio falls to an effective value $r_{\mathrm{eff}}<r$, while the shielded rear jet rises above the reference. This paper identifies the carrier of that dilution and the unsteady dynamics that sustains it. The rear-jet blockage closes a gap recirculation whose reversed flow puts the two gap-side layers in the counter-current shear-layer configuration, the classical route to enhanced entrainment. The measured Reynolds stress and Prandtl mixing length show that the absolute exchange is nearly independent of the velocity ratio and exceeds the single-jet leeward zone like-for-like by up to $1.5\times$ (zone peak, across conditions) and $2.8\times$ (area-integrated) at $r\approx7$. The gain comes from an enlarged mixing scale rather than from a steeper shear, and the front-jet near-field shortening follows the absolute exchange transport rather than the twin/single enhancement ratio. The turbulent term exceeds the pressure term in eight of the nine conditions, and the flux budget reads the dilution as a limited mass addition plus a momentum loss to the crossflow; the evidence remains observational. The gap-side layers remain convectively unstable---DMD and SPOD find no growing mode within the resolvable band and record length---so the exchange is carried by convecting vortex trains rather than by a self-excited global mode.
label: physics.flu-dyn

description: A Resource Allocation Tournament. We introduce and analyze a round-robin simultaneous resource allocation contest, motivated by sports leagues and other competitive environments where agents must distribute limited resources across multiple encounters. Players allocate resources in advance to matches against all opponents, and match outcomes are determined by relative allocations. We study two payoff schemes: total points, where players accumulate rewards for each win, and winner-takes-all, where only the tournament winner is rewarded. For three players, we provide complete equilibrium characterizations under both schemes. For four or more players, we show that the total points payoff admits Blotto-type equilibria, while the winner-takes-all payoff requires numerical and algorithmic analysis. To address this, we develop a best-response dynamics algorithm with stochastic inertia and use it to approximate equilibria in games with four and five players.
label: math.OC

description: How Well Do Decision Models Transfer to Vietnamese? An Empirical Study of Text Classification. Recent advances in specialized decision models have expanded the possibilities for zero-shot classification, yet their effectiveness on Vietnamese remains underexplored. This study evaluates four specialized decision models across 13 classification settings spanning six task groups, examining zero-shot performance, sensitivity to label-description language, and robustness to Vietnamese linguistic variations. The evaluation considers English, Vietnamese, and bilingual label descriptions, alongside common linguistic perturbations involving teencode, typographical errors, and diacritic removal. Under English label descriptions, JEV achieves the strongest overall performance, ranking first in 11 classification settings. The effects of label-description language vary across models and datasets, with bilingual descriptions providing no consistent improvement. Robustness experiments reveal that diacritic removal causes the most substantial performance degradation, reducing mean macro-$F_1$ by 9.51--15.47 points across model configurations, considerably more than teencode or typographical errors. These findings highlight the importance of label-description choices and Vietnamese orthographic variation when evaluating specialized decision models for zero-shot text classification.
label: cs.CL

description: Modulation theory of Y- and X-wave Kadomtsev--Petviashvili solitons. The evolution of long wavelength perturbations of traveling wave 2-soliton solutions of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili II (KP) equation are investigated using modulation theory. An initial-boundary value problem for a system of hyperbolic conservation laws is formulated for amplitude and slope perturbations to soliton legs of the resonant (Y-shaped) and X-shaped KP traveling wave solutions. The vertex where individuated soliton legs coalesce is modeled as a moving free boundary where information between the soliton legs can pass. The linearized hyperbolic system is proven to be well-posed under suitable initial conditions and is solved exactly. In the case of the resonant Y-shaped soliton, all admissible simple (rarefaction) waves of the nonlinear system are characterized. Specific perturbations of Y-waves can lead to the dimensionality of the modulated solution changing, corresponding to a physical geometric change to the multi-soliton pattern. Spontaneous leg deletion and leg creation can occur. The conditions under which the Y-wave modulation system can experience gradient catastrophe are given. Gradient catastrophe is regularized by the formation of a new leg, with an augmented modulation system proposed to describe the growth of the new leg. On the other hand, the X-wave system can be reduced to two independent line soliton modulation systems. These findings reinforce the prevalence and generality of resonant Y-shaped vertices in the KP II system and applications.The theoretical modulation predictions are supported by direct numerical simulations of KP II, which show good agreement with the analysis.
label: nlin.PS

description: A superconducting LC resonator in a multi-tesla magnetic field for tabletop kHz gravitational-wave detection. We present a concept for a superconducting inductance--capacitance (LC) resonator immersed in a magnetic field for gravitational-wave detection in the kHz band. In the long-wavelength limit, a gravitational wave in a static magnetic field induces an oscillating magnetic-field perturbation proportional to the static magnetic field applied to the resonator and to the gravitational-wave strain. We show that a superconducting pickup circuit can convert this perturbation into a flux signal read out by a superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID)-based or quantum-limited amplifier chain. Inspired by resonant-mass detectors, we develop a three-loop coupled-circuit model and derive the equivalent strain-noise spectrum, including thermal noise, SQUID backaction, and measurement imprecision. Prototype measurements demonstrate a quality factor of $Q\simeq 5\times 10^5$, while $Q=10^7$ is considered as a future development target. Under the assumed flux coupling and an idealized quantum-limited SQUID noise model, optimized circuits yield projected strain sensitivities of order $10^{-21}\,\mathrm{Hz}^{-1/2}$ over $100\,\mathrm{Hz}$ bands in the $1$--$20\,\mathrm{kHz}$ range. Increasing the active high-field volume and improving quantum-limited readout could enable further sensitivity gains. This compact, tunable detector concept could complement interferometric gravitational-wave searches and motivate investigations of high-frequency astrophysical sources.
label: hep-ex

description: Dimension-free regimes for unadjusted Langevin in ridge-separable models: A subspace robust Wasserstein analysis. The Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm (ULA) is widely used for high-dimensional Bayesian inference. Classical analyses in Wasserstein-2 distance predict an asymptotic bias and a mixing time that grow with dimension, but this metric is stronger than necessary for many statistical tasks. We instead analyze the bias in subspace robust Wasserstein distance, which controls the mean and arbitrary low-dimensional marginals and is therefore well suited to observables typically estimated in practice. For ridge-separable potentials formed with i.i.d. data, we prove high-probability bounds showing a bell-shaped mixing profile as the number of data points $N$ varies relative to the dimension $d$. In the overparameterized regime, the effective dimension is the rank $N$ of the data-dependent perturbation, leading to complexity depending on $N$ rather than $d$. In the large-sample regime, Gaussian-perturbation estimates yield dimension-free complexity once $N$ is sufficiently large. In contrast, near the proportional regime $\asymp d$, we prove that dimension-free guarantees are impossible in general.
label: stat.ML

description: PerMix: Anomalous sound detection by predicting the perturbation ratio of mixed samples. In anomalous sound detection based on self-supervised learning, the performance of the detection model largely depends on the selection of the pretext task through which the characteristics of normal data are learned. A common pretext task is to mix samples from different classes and classify the mixed sample as its target class with an angular margin loss. However, this supervision becomes mismatched when the target sample is the minority component of the mixture and the margin remains fixed irrespective of the mixing ratio. To address these issues, we propose a pretext task that directly predicts the perturbation ratio of mixed samples by reformulating the logit so that the angular margin is scaled by the perturbation ratio. In addition, we adopt a supervised contrastive loss modified for mixed samples, in which positive pairs are formed according to the dominant class. Experiments show that our approach achieves state-of-the-art results on the DCASE 2020 Task 2 benchmark. Our code is available at https://github.com/kaistss/PerMix.
label: eess.AS

description: Homomorphic Encryption with Coset Code Construction. Homomorphic encryption enables computation on input data without decrypting it. This paper extends a construction based on scalar message codes, utilizing coset codes to pack $k$ message symbols into a ciphertext vector of length $n$. For a given field and vector length, this packing method reduces the number of ciphertext vectors required to transmit a message record. A compatible family of evaluation codes supports public addition and multiplication operations up to a predetermined degree. We prove that the scheme achieves bounded chosen-plaintext security under the coordinate-label distinguishability assumption.
label: cs.IT

description: Multi-Token Prediction and Alternative Tokenization Improve Learning Latent Multi-Hop Graph Search at Scale. Given an unseen graph, a start node, $s$, and an end node, $t$, can a language model generate the shortest path from $s$ to $t$? Prior work has found that models fail to learn this task as the graphs scale. We show that this failure has two causes: the supervision signal and the tokenization. First, we theoretically establish and empirically demonstrate the effectiveness of multi-token prediction (MTP), and show that the benefits of MTP are topologically agnostic. Second, we introduce alternative tokenizations and show that the two causes are orthogonal. Using these methods, we break through the scaling wall observed by prior work, consistently and stably learning to solve the task at scales far beyond previous limits.
label: cs.LG

description: Random Survivor Sets with Moving Holes in Bedford-McMullen Carpets. Let $2\le m < n$ be integers, and let $K(\mathcal{A})$ be the Bedford--McMullen carpet generated by $\{(x,y)\mapsto((x+i)/m,(y+j)/n):(i,j)\in\mathcal{A}\}$, where $\mathcal{A}$ is a subset of $\{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}\times\{0,1,\ldots,n-1\}$. Write $\mathcal{B}$ for the set of occupied columns, and assume that $\#\mathcal{B}\ge2$ and each column contains at least two symbols of $\mathcal{A}$. At each vertex of the column tree $\mathcal{B}^*$, we independently choose one forbidden symbol from $\mathcal{A}$ according to a prescribed distribution. Let $\mathbb{P}$ denote the resulting product measure on $\mathcal{A}^{\mathcal{B}^*}$. This gives a random survivor set $K_ω(\mathcal{A})$ with $ω\in\mathcal{A}^{\mathcal{B}^*}$. We show that, for $\mathbb{P}$-a.e. $ω$, \begin{equation*} \dim_H K_ω(\mathcal{A})=\frac{1}{\log m}\log\left(\int \sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}}\ell_b(ω)^{\frac{\log m}{\log n}} d\mathbb{P}(ω)\right), \end{equation*} where $\ell_b(ω)$ is the number of surviving symbols in column $b$ at the root.
label: math.DS

description: Gravitational Wave Diffractive Images Reveal the Structure of Astrophysical Objects. Scattering patterns encode the structure of extended objects, as demonstrated by charged particle scattering on atomic nuclei. Gravitational wave (GW) diffraction offers an analogous probe of otherwise invisible mass distributions. At linear order in the lens potential we derive expressions relating the central diffractive image contribution to a gravitationally lensed GW waveform to the Fourier transform of the projected lens density. For finite mass lenses this contribution takes the form of a point mass Born amplitude multiplied by a normalized mass form factor, analogous to that in nuclear scattering. As the frequency of GWs from a merging compact binary source evolves the signal samples this form factor across spatial scales, imprinting lens structure through interference with the primary image. Using full numerical wave optics calculations we quantify the observational reach for extended dark matter objects, primordial black holes halo-dressed by dark matter halos and superradiance clouds of ultralight bosons around black holes. For the considered source populations, five year observations with next generation detectors can distinguish extended lenses from point masses, probing dark matter fractions down to $\mathcal{O}(10^{-5})$, and halo-dressed primordial black holes from matched bare black holes, probing primordial black hole dark matter fractions down to $\mathcal{O}(10^{-6})$. For sufficiently close source-lens configurations, scalar superradiance clouds can produce distinguishable diffraction signatures for boson masses of approximately $10^{-17}-10^{-12}~\mathrm{eV}$. These results provide a framework for characterizing extended dark matter and compact object astrophysical environments.
label: astro-ph.CO

description: Local heights for nef toric compactified divisors. We present a definition of a local height of nef toric divisors in the sense of Yuan and Zhang by approximating a height for canonical divisors and then using the local energy to extend to other metrics on the same geometric divisor.
label: math.AG

description: ConQEC: Concolic Testing for Quantum Error-Correcting Code Implementations. Quantum error-correcting code (QECC) implementations are hybrid software-control systems: measured syndromes drive decoder dispatch, recovery actions, and logical checks. Existing QECC verification techniques can prove formal obligations, and general quantum testing can expose final failures, but developers still lack a scalable testing workflow that generates concrete faults and explains where a QECC repair path first diverges. This paper presents ConQEC, to our knowledge the first concolic testing framework for QECC implementations. By combining concrete (Pauli) fault replay with symbolic repair-path constraints, ConQEC generates tests that expose not only final logical failures but also fault--syndrome--decoder--recovery (FSDR) diagnostics: the injected fault, observed syndrome, decoder decision, recovery action, oracle result, and earliest divergent stage. Its symbolic encoding of Pauli faults, syndrome predicates, decoder and recovery relations, and oracle checks enables this diagnostic workflow to scale beyond exponentially increasing amplitude-level quantum-state reasoning. We implemented ConQEC and evaluated it on generated source-level QECC families and public QECC artifacts with up to thousands of qubits. ConQEC detects the seeded bug in every experimental case and reports a replay-valid, fault-localizing FSDR witness for each.
label: quant-ph

description: Procrustes-Bering-Sheaft: Automated Model Discovery and Virtual Crash Tests for Microservices. Procrustes-Bering-Sheaft automates lightweight model discovery and virtual crash tests for microservices. Each test estimates operation availability by Monte Carlo sampling of service and communication failures. Procrustes checks deployment and tracing evidence; Bering discovers dependencies and incorporates replica declarations; Sheaft evaluates declared operation-success conditions. Independent command-line interfaces exchange reusable, versioned artifacts. The toolchain extends an earlier graph-based approach with mandatory-call contracts, failure-tolerance sweeps, baseline comparison, component-importance analysis, and CI/CD gates. We demonstrate the workflow on one HTTP operation. Six controlled execution states exposed two mismatches between reachability and observed success; an explicit required-call predicate matched all six. Two modelled one-replica additions produced different decisions: recommendation retained an availability-target violation, whereas catalog restored the baseline estimate of 0.979900 and grid tolerance of 0.12. Analytical oracles and controlled tests verify the implementation; archived replay checks numerical continuity with two earlier studies.
label: cs.SE

description: Peak-Aware One-Way Trading: Competitive and Learning-Augmented Algorithms for Energy Procurement. We introduce peak-aware one-way trading ($\texttt{PA-OWT}$), an online problem in which a player must purchase a fixed quantity of an asset by a deadline, minimizing its total cost plus a charge proportional to the largest single purchase at any time. The model is motivated by electricity procurement, where the cost of energy rewards buying at low prices, but peak demand charges discourage concentrating purchases in short periods. Balancing these incentives is challenging when future prices are unknown: a large purchase can establish a peak that later decisions cannot undo. We develop a peak-aware online algorithm that balances price and peak control with deadline feasibility and achieves the order-optimal competitive ratio. We further extend our results to a learning-augmented algorithm that uses predictions of optimal purchasing decisions to achieve an order-optimal consistency-robustness tradeoff, exploiting accurate advice while retaining worst-case guarantees in the face of arbitrary prediction errors. Finally, we evaluate our algorithms in a case study on electricity procurement using historical electricity price traces to understand the benefits of peak-aware purchasing.
label: cs.DS

description: Concentration inequalities for vector-valued martingales. In this paper, we establish several deviation inequalities for the norms of vector-valued martingales, achieving bounds of the same quality as those available in the classical one-dimensional setting. Our results extend and refine previous work by Pinelis (1994) and Hayes (2005) in this area.
label: math.PR

description: Nanopillar metasurfaces uniting high optical reflectivity with ultracoherent nanomechanics. Mechanically compliant mirrors are key components in cavity optomechanics. However, the requirements to achieve the best optical and mechanical performance are usually in direct competition. A high reflectivity for tightly focused beams entails thick reflectors, whereas ultracoherent flexural nanomechanics necessitates thin membranes. We eliminate this trade-off by introducing high-refractive-index nanopillar metasurfaces on top of a thin membrane. We pattern a 50 micrometer-diameter array of nanopillars to form a photonic crystal. The flat band behavior of guided resonances in the photonic crystal enables a reflectivity of 99.82(1)% for a tightly focused beam of 7 micrometer waist. The combination of two guided resonances creates a 100 nanometer-wide high-reflectivity band around 1550 nanometer. Simultaneously, the nanopillar patterning realizes a density-modulated phononic crystal that isolates an ultracoherent localized mechanical mode with a $Q\cdot f$-product of $2\cdot 10^{14}$Hz. The demonstrated nanopillar metasurfaces enable lightweight mirrors for room-temperature quantum optomechanics and for use as levitated mirrors or lightsails.
label: physics.optics

description: Concavity-Free $L^\infty$ Estimates and Stability for Fully Nonlinear Complex Equations. In this paper, we extend the $L^\infty$ estimates of Guo-Phong for fully non-linear equations on compact hermitian manifolds to a possibly indefinite reference form satisfying a uniform admissibility criterion. Furthermore, we also establish one-sided stability estimates. Neither result requires homogeneity or concavity of the nonlinear operator.
label: math.DG

description: Unexpected Local Enhancement of Chromospheric Moreton Waves on the Sun. Solar eruptions often drive shock waves. When propagating in the solar corona, strong shock waves would leave imprints on the solar surface in the chromosphere, which are called Moreton waves. Moreton waves generally decay as they move away. However, to our knowledge, for the first time we report that a Moreton wave is significantly enhanced midway during propagation, as revealed by the spectroscopic observations from China's first solar satellite, the Chinese H$α$ Solar Explorer. Combining magnetic measurements from the Solar Dynamics Observatory, we found that the location of the Moreton wave enhancement corresponds to a magnetic null point at an altitude of $\sim$70 Mm in the corona. It is demonstrated that the unexpected local enhancement of the Moreton wave is due to mode conversion around the magnetic null point, i.e., fast-mode waves are converted to slow-mode waves which are trapped locally. It is further revealed that, even for ordinary Moreton wave fronts, the H$α$ Doppler redshift velocity is positively correlated with the height of widespread low-altitude magnetic null points, implying that these low-lying null points, $\sim$1--7 Mm above the solar surface, facilitate mode conversion with different efficiency, thereby accounting for the spatially inhomogeneous Dopplergram of Moreton wave fronts.
label: astro-ph.SR

description: Evidence for Kaluza-Klein excitations of the graviton, gluon and quark at LHC. Following our paper showing evidence for a sequence of Kaluza-Klein gravitons, we interpret the massive 4 jet excesses observed by CMS in RUN2 and RUN3 data. They could come from the decay of two heavy KK gluons gkk(3.6TeV) and gkk(8.6TeV) into pairs of KK quarks qkk(1TeV) and qkk(2.1TeV). Present limits on gkk seem to exclude gkk(3.6TeV) but these limits assume a dominant decay into top pairs, which can be questioned as was the case in our study of KK graviton decays. The cross section predicted for gkk(8.6) requires a BR into a pair of qkk(2.1TeV) or order 10% which is not unlikely. Prospect for reaching a 6 s.d. level local evidence with RUN3 data are promising for 3 channels.
label: hep-ph

description: How Different, or Different How? Stance Granularity in Viewpoint Selection for Dialog Systems that Engage Users with Alternative Views. Systems that aim to help a user engage with viewpoints other than their own have to decide how different those viewpoints should be. Viewpoints are mainly represented on a scalar scale, too coarse to distinguish viewpoints that disagree with the user about different things. We introduce a selection policy in which a bandit sets how far viewpoints may sit from the user, and the policy selects the most novel viewpoint within that bound. We vary only its stance encoder, comparing a scalar score with Perspectivized Stance Vectors, which break a position into separate stances on concepts. We integrate it inside a dialog system and run a between-subjects study (N=63). Concept-level stance produces more varied exposure sequences and broader coverage of the topic's positions, but does not change how deeply users justify viewpoints or how accurately they reconstruct them. Finally, we analyze user--viewpoint relations at the concept level, showing that users reconstruct a viewpoint least accurately on concepts that one side took no position on, rather than on concepts where the two disagreed. Our findings open up opportunities for dialog systems that support engagement with alternative viewpoints by acting on which concepts a user and a viewpoint disagree on, rather than on distance alone.
label: cs.HC

description: Deep holes of full-length Reed--Solomon codes: uniform bounds and exact classifications. Let $u$ be a received word for the full-length Reed--Solomon code $\operatorname{RS}_q(k)$, with interpolation polynomial $f_u$ of degree $k+m$. For each $m\in\{3,4,5,6,7\}$, we classify all such deep holes over every finite field, without a field-size hypothesis. None occur for odd $m$ in this range. At $m=4$ and $m=6$, the only exceptions are, respectively, the Segre sextic and Frobenius-power families; these occur only in dimension two over fields of characteristic two. For arbitrary $m\geqslant3$, we also establish two uniform bounds. If $\sqrt q\geqslant12(m+1)\log(2m+2)$, no word of interpolation degree $k+m$ is a deep hole when $q$ is odd, $k\geqslant3$, or $m$ is odd. If $q>16(m+2)^4$, we obtain the corresponding complete classification at every admissible $k$, including the explicit dimension-two exceptions. Our proofs use an agreement criterion expressed in complete homogeneous symmetric functions, agreement-count estimates, finite geometry, permutation-polynomial restrictions, and subset constructions for solving the resulting symmetric-function equations. The remaining finite cases are settled by finite computations with supplied certificates and deterministic verification programs.
label: cs.IT

description: Uniform coarse ellipticity, $A_2$ weights, and boundary regularity. We study symmetric divergence form elliptic equations with measurable coefficients that may be degenerate and unbounded, under a uniform bound on the coarse ellipticity ratio over all ambient cubes and scales. We prove that uniform coarse ellipticity and classical $A_2$ weighted ellipticity define incomparable coefficient classes. For every admissible choice of coarse parameters, we construct a scalar weight with a logarithmically corrected, locally integrable singularity along a product Cantor set. Its codimension is chosen according to the upper coarse discount exponent, and the resulting coefficient satisfies the uniform coarse condition but is comparable to no $A_2$ weight. Conversely, an explicit $A_2$ weight fails the coarse condition for every admissible parameter choice. Under uniform coarse ellipticity we give a direct PDE treatment of boundary regularity in the approximable energy realization. Using coarse interior estimates, we prove boundary decay and solvability of the continuous Dirichlet problem in bounded NTA domains. An almost-positivity argument, with energy approximation and boundary testing justified, yields boundary Harnack and Hölder continuity of quotients of positive solutions with common zero boundary values. The argument requires no additional energy Sobolev inequality and avoids the construction of Green functions. Further examples distinguish uniform coarse control from finite coefficient moments and from coercivity on $\mathrm L^2(\mathrm{d} x)$. We also record interior Hölder estimates and continuity criteria under nonuniform control along nested scales.
label: math.AP

description: Pólya's conjecture for Neumann eigenvalues of spherical shells. We prove the strict Pólya inequality for Neumann eigenvalues of spherical shells in every dimension $d\ge2$, for every radius ratio and every positive energy. The proof also covers balls. For shells, the excess over the leading Weyl term has a positive lower bound depending only on dimension. Above explicit frequency thresholds independent of the radius ratio, we obtain a surplus of boundary order. These estimates remain uniform as the hole shrinks or the shell becomes thin. We compare weighted sampling errors for inverse radial actions while retaining the removed volume exactly. The proof is entirely analytic and requires no computer-assisted verification.
label: math.SP

description: From Structured Records to Patient Narratives: Preserving Clinical Alignment in LLM-Generated Health Summaries. As wearable and digital health systems increasingly generate longitudinal physiological records, communicating these observations in patient-accessible language remains a significant challenge. Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a promising mechanism for translating structured clinical information into readable narratives, but this process may introduce semantic drift, where clinically precise meaning is distorted during simplification. We investigate evidence-grounded health summarization for menstrual health monitoring using a constrained generation framework that combines structured evidence conditioning with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) using a prompt-based constrained generation framework. We evaluate semantic alignment using Natural Language Inference (NLI), atomic factuality metrics, and readability measures. Across three LLMs and 4,500 generated summaries, explicit grounding constraints consistently improve clinical alignment, particularly by improving uncertainty preservation and, once faithfulness is evaluated against retrieved evidence, generally preserving or improving faithfulness, while effects on omission remain model-dependent. We also find that improved clinical alignment comes at the cost of increased reading difficulty and medical terminology. These findings highlight the need to jointly evaluate faithfulness, uncertainty preservation, and readability when developing patient-facing medical LLM systems.
label: cs.CL

description: QUIJOTE scientific results - XII. Characterization of the polarized synchrotron emission at the power spectrum level in the QUIJOTE-MFI wide survey. We present an analysis of the polarized synchrotron emission at the power-spectrum level in the multipole range $30 20^\circ$, hinting toward a steepening of the BB spectrum relative to EE at the $\sim 1.6σ$ level. The synchrotron frequency spectral indices are found to be $β_s^{EE} = -3.26 \pm 0.05$ and $β_s^{BB} = -3.25 \pm 0.10$ for the same cut, in agreement with earlier real-space analyses. We find no evidence for spatial variations of $β_s$ across different Galactic latitude cuts, within current uncertainties. The synchrotron BB/EE power ratio is approximately 0.2 over the considered multipole range, lower than typical values for thermal dust, and consistent with previous measurements. We also measure a dust-synchrotron spatial correlation in the range 0.1-0.25 over $30 < \ell < 130$. Using these results, we estimate the level of synchrotron contamination in future CMB B-mode measurements, finding an average power in the considered sky masks equivalent to $r \sim 0.003$ at 90GHz and $r \sim 0.0002$ at 150GHz for the relevant angular scales.
label: astro-ph.CO

description: Measuring the Verifier's Floor: How Much Apparent Rare-Word Text-to-Speech Error Is ASR Error?. Text-to-speech (TTS) is usually evaluated by transcribing its output with an automatic speech recognition (ASR) system, so the word error rate also counts recognizer errors. We measure these errors on human recordings of the test sentences. On LibriSpeech and FLEURS, the evaluation recognizer misses 33-67% of very rare words even in human speech, and all three recognizers miss 22-42%. Checking every word with two more recognizer families lowers the apparent TTS error on words that at least one recognizer hears two- to three-fold (very rare LibriSpeech words: from 10-13% to 3-5%), yet very rare words remain the hardest. Ignoring words the recognizer misses in human speech is biased: the other recognizers find TTS errors far more often on these words (4-6% vs. 0.2-0.3%) and overturn about half of the errors this mask keeps. As half of the remaining adjudicated errors may be spelling variants, a listening test is needed.
label: cs.SD

description: Chaotic dynamics and resonances in Einstein-Rosen standing wave spacetimes. Recent work has revealed chaotic geodesic behavior in Einstein-Rosen standing gravitational wave spacetimes. The dynamics of massive test particles are dominated by chaotic heteroclinic networks. This study demonstrates that the dynamical structure of the system is far richer than previously thought. Applying the subharmonic Melnikov function method to Poincaré maps reveals the admissible types of heteroclinic networks. I trace the evolution of these structures under the continuous change of the solution's parameters. In this way, I identify bifurcation phenomena, including a period-doubling bifurcation.
label: gr-qc

description: Prime Nullspace Matrices and Even Dominating Sets. A non-zero $m \times n$ (0, 1)-matrix $A$ is called a {\em nullspace matrix} if each entry $(i, j)$ of $A$ has an even number of $1's$ in the set of entries consisting of $(i, j)$ and its rectilinear neighbors. These matrices correspond to even dominating sets of $m \times n$ grid graphs. We study these matrices and consider those that cannot be constructed from smaller nullspace matrices.
label: math.CO

description: Asymptotic observable symmetry for spacetime observability of waves I: The disc. Building on the spacetime observable symmetry discovered in NWX (2025), we introduce asymptotic observable symmetry (AOS) for the wave equation. Its central object is a family of generated approximate velocities constructed from fixed profiles, carrying the same propagation-induced symmetry at different scales and asymptotically realized by exact waves. We investigate AOS on the disc through radial propagation and reflection. This gives a family of spacetime measurable observation sets satisfying the essential spacetime measurable geometric control condition for a fixed positive observation time. However, the observability inequality fails on each of these fixed sets.
label: math.AP

description: Homogenization of the Stokes equations with slender bodies. In this paper we study the convergence of solutions of the Stokes equations in a domain perforated by slender bodies placed on a fixed periodic grid of size $2ε$ as the size of the bodies goes to zero and the number of bodies goes to infinity. We assume that the width $b_ε$ of the bodies vanishes faster than the length $a_ε$ of the particles. We identify the critical scaling regimes for $a_ε$ and $b_ε$ and prove that in this case the system is effectively described by the Brinkman equations.
label: math.AP

description: Supporting or Replacing Students' Reasoning? Cognitive Offloading in AI-Assisted Proof Learning. We studied 153 students in an undergraduate proof-based mathematics course with staggered-access to an AI support system. Students were randomly assigned to receive an AI chatbot and a homework-feedback interface earlier or later in the course. During the period when only the early-access group had access, their homework scores were 2.56 points higher, but exam performance did not differ significantly between groups, suggesting that improved AI-supported homework performance did not translate into detectable gains on a subsequent exam. After all students received access, every additional 100 messages sent to the AI chatbot was associated with a 3.02-point lower score on the subsequent exam. A mediation analysis showed a significant indirect association linking lower baseline self-efficacy to greater chatbot use and, in turn, lower exam scores: a one-point decrease in self-efficacy corresponded to 0.62 fewer exam points through chatbot use. These findings raise concerns that students may use the chatbot to offload their cognitive reasoning. Use of the homework-feedback interface, which required students to submit their proof attempts before receiving feedback, was not negatively associated with exam performance. We recommend against using a chatbot for AI tutoring and suggest exploring a tutor embedded in the course activities.
label: cs.HC

description: Slow Massive-Star Formation and the O-Star ZAMS Deficit. The scarcity of optically visible O stars near the theoretical zero-age main sequence (ZAMS) has puzzled astronomers for over four decades. We argue that it reflects prolonged accretion. If massive stars assemble over Myr timescales, as the inertial-inflow model predicts, core-hydrogen burning begins before accretion ends, and the stars become optically visible at the end of accretion on a birthline displaced from the standard ZAMS. We test this interpretation by comparing the hot-side envelope of Galactic O stars in the Kiel diagram with accreting stellar-evolution models, adopting a growth law $t_{\mathrm{form}}=τ_0(m_{\mathrm{f}}/60 M_\odot)^α$ with formation time $t_{\mathrm{form}}$ and final mass $m_{\mathrm{f}}$. The resulting birthlines reproduce both the displacement and the high-mass turnover of the observed envelope, with best-fitting parameters $(α,τ_0)=(0.52,4.3\,\mathrm{Myr})$, consistent with independent constraints from the luminosity functions of compact H II regions and OB stars. The two constraints have orthogonal degeneracy directions, so combining them narrows the allowed parameter space, yielding projected 90% confidence intervals $0.43<α<0.60$ and $3.9<τ_0/\mathrm{Myr}<5.0$. The inferred growth law agrees with cloud-scale simulations and the inertial-inflow model, and implies that mass assembly and main-sequence evolution overlap substantially in massive stars, with broader implications for stellar evolution and feedback.
label: astro-ph.SR

description: Effective Dual Subgradient Methods Through Sequential Subgradient-Aligned Rays. In this paper, we propose an efficient subgradient-based framework, referred to as the sequential subgradient-aligned rays (SSAR) method, for improving the convergence performance of the dual subgradient method. In particular, the proposed method identifies and exploits a finite sequence of rays, when available, as the dual subgradient method evolves, along each of which a subgradient of the negative dual function remains constant and aligns with the ray. While the dual variable iterates remain on each identified ray, a constant stepsize associated with the ray is employed, with the associated constant stepsizes decreasing from one ray to the next. This approach yields constant decrements in the negative dual function values while the dual variable iterates remain on the associated rays, enabling the dual variable iterates to progress more quickly toward a dual optimal solution. We then show that the proposed SSAR method can be leveraged to improve the performance of the dual decomposition method for minimizing the average of local loss functions associated with multiple agents that share a common decision variable, a widely used problem formulation in many large-scale real-world applications. In particular, the SSAR method improves the convergence performance of the corresponding dual decomposition method while also reducing its communication cost. Numerical experiments on a least squares regression problem and a logistic regression problem using real datasets are conducted to evaluate the performance of the SSAR method.
label: math.OC

description: Self-Supervised Multibeam Sonar Restoration via Coherent Forward Modeling. Multibeam imaging sonar produces intensity images degraded by coherent speckle and system-induced blur, while clean reflectivity targets are rarely available. Existing despeckling methods often rely on simplified intensity-domain noise models, synthetic clean targets, or blind-spot self-supervision, and typically do not jointly model deblurring and speckle suppression. We propose a physics-consistent self-supervised framework for joint despeckling and deblurring of multibeam imaging sonar. A stochastic coherent image-formation model yields a conditional-mean forward operator that relates latent scene reflectivity to expected intensity through the squared magnitude of the system point spread function. We then use registered multi-frame sonar sequences to train without clean ground truth images, showing that, under an idealized inter-frame conditional-mean condition, the expected paired loss equals the corresponding forward-prediction loss up to a network-independent constant. To stabilize the ill-conditioned inverse problem, we further adapt robust equivariant imaging using stochastic coherent simulation and introduce a paired forward prediction error metric for ground-truth-free evaluation. Experiments on two real multibeam sonar datasets demonstrate a favourable balance between forward-prediction agreement, homogeneous-region speckle suppression, and preservation of visible structural boundaries compared with representative baselines.
label: eess.IV

description: Coresets for $k$-Means: When Does Uniform Sampling Suffice?. Data summarization techniques, such as coresets, are essential for scaling clustering algorithms to massive datasets. We study uniform sampling, which is an extremely simple and ultra-efficient method to construct coresets, in the context of weak, stable, and strong coresets for the $k$-means problem in Hilbert space. We begin with the fundamental case $k=1$, and establish matching upper and lower bounds on the sample complexity of stable and weak coresets, finding that the two notions require different sample complexities. As a consequence, we obtain tight bounds for stable $1$-median coresets in $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ (and thus also Kendall--tau and Jaccard metrics), removing the dimension dependence of Carmel and Krauthgamer (ICLR 2026). Our analysis is substantially simpler than prior work and reduces to bounding the deviation of the sample mean. For the general $k$-means problem on $ρ$-separated instances, a well-studied structural assumption on the input, we show that uniform sampling yields a stable coreset for all $O(1)$-approximate solutions, and a strong coreset if the instance additionally has bounded kurtosis. In all these results, the sample complexity is independent of the dimension and the instance size.
label: cs.DS

description: Improved Bounds for the Entropic Central Limit Theorem in the Log-Concave Case. Let $μ$ be a log-concave isotropic probability measure on $R^d$ , and let $μ^n$ denote the law of the normalized sum of $n$ independent random vectors with law $μ$. We prove that \[ H(μ^n|γ)\leq \frac{C}{n} \min\left\{1+\log(ed)^2H(μ|γ)\ ,\ d\right\}. \] Compared to the previous best known bound, our estimate replaces the polynomial dependence on the dimension by a polylogarithmic one. The proof relies on a new combination of the De Bruijn identity with Eldan's stochastic localization process.
label: cs.IT

description: A semiampleness result for hyperkähler fourfolds and smoothings of Lagrangian subvarieties. We give a geometric proof of the following statement: let $X$ be a smooth hyperkähler fourfold such that the Picard group is generated by a line bundle $L$ that is nef, non-trivial, and not big. If the Kodaira dimension of $L$ is non-negative, some positive multiple defines a Lagrangian fibration. The proof requires a number of tools which are of independent interest, including an analogue of Voisin's unobstructedness result and a smoothing result for singular Lagrangian subvarieties.
label: math.AG

description: Observation of Polarization Topology in Magneto-Optical BICs. Polarization topology in momentum space is a fundamental characteristic of photonic bound states in the continuum (BICs), where the winding of far-field polarization defines a quantized topological charge. Although magneto-optical (MO) BICs combine polarization topology with magnetically tunable chirality, experimental characterization remains challenging because time-reversal symmetry (TRS) breaking complicates eigenpolarization extraction. Here, we experimentally resolve the momentum-space polarization topology of an MO BIC by reconstructing its two-dimensional far-field eigenpolarization texture. We extract the resonant output polarization using singular value decomposition of the polarization-resolved angle-resolved reflection matrix without invoking reciprocity. The reconstructed polarization azimuth winds counterclockwise by 2$π$ around the $Γ$-point singularity, yielding a topological charge of q = +1. Moreover, the polarization handedness can be reversed solely by varying the magnetic-bias strength, while the field direction and the measured topological charge remain unchanged. A non-Hermitian coupled-mode model traces this reversal to hybridization between the BIC mode and a leaky mode. This work establishes experimental access to momentum-space polarization topology in nonreciprocal photonics, opening a route to explore topological singularities and their evolution under active TRS breaking.
label: physics.optics

description: Water Transport on 3-Spiders: Unbounded Lengths of Shortest Optimal Strategies. Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. An averaging operation selects a nonempty connected vertex set and replaces the weights of its vertices by their arithmetic mean. For a nonnegative initial weight function $ω:V(G)\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ and a target vertex $x$, let $t(G,x,ω)$ denote the minimum number of averaging operations needed to attain the maximum reachable weight at $x$. Gollin et al.[1] proved, using the Axiom of Choice, that a finite optimal strategy exists for every finite graph, every nonnegative initial weight function and every target vertex; see Tao [2] for a simplified proof. We prove that the lengths of shortest optimal strategies on $3$-spiders have no uniform finite bound. In particular, these lengths cannot be bounded in terms of the maximum degree of the graph.
label: math.CO

description: Douglas-Rachford splitting method for nonconvex stochastic optimal control. Motivated by the numerical resolution of stochastic optimal control problems, particularly those involving nonlinear dynamics, we investigate the convergence properties of the Douglas-Rachford splitting algorithm in a nonconvex and infinite-dimensional setting. We introduce an extension of the method that applies when one component of the objective function is continuously differentiable with a locally Lipschitz gradient, while the other is weakly lower semicontinuous with a bounded domain.
label: math.OC

description: Maximum Likelihood Estimation and Likelihood Ratio Tests for the Power Spherical Distribution. The Power Spherical distribution has been proposed as a computationally efficient alternative to the von Mises-Fisher distribution for data on the unit sphere, with reduced computational cost for simulation and a simpler normalizing constant. Despite these advantages, its statistical inference properties remain underdeveloped. In this paper, we develop a likelihood-based framework for estimation and inference for the Power Spherical distribution. Within this framework, we develop maximum likelihood estimation procedures for both the central direction and concentration parameter. Building on these estimators, we formulate likelihood ratio tests for hypotheses involving known and unknown parameters, study their asymptotic behavior, and evaluate finite-sample performance through simulation studies. The results demonstrate accurate Type I error control and good power when the asymptotic chi-square approximation is appropriate, while the parametric bootstrap provides reliable inference in small-sample settings or those where the dimension is large relative to the sample size. The findings also highlight nontrivial dependence of the power of tests for the central direction on the concentration parameter.
label: stat.ME

description: FairFRESH: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Fair and Explainable Household Food Recommendation. Recommender systems typically serve one user at a time. However, in households, members share a finite pantry and follow different dietary rules, making independent recommendations prone to resource conflicts and dietary violations. We formulate household food recommendation as constrained fair division and present FairFRESH, a neuro-symbolic framework that learns per-member utilities, allocates foods under explicit welfare objectives, enforces dietary rules through a deterministic filter, and explains recommendations using Shapley and Banzhaf attributions. Theoretically, we show that no finite penalty guarantees compliance near a dietary-rule threshold, establish approximation guarantees for greedy allocation under utilitarian and smoothed Nash objectives in the stock-free model before filtering, and characterize the scale invariance of Nash welfare. We also use the minimax theorem to analyze rotating shared meals. On NHANES-derived data, the learned utility model achieves Recall@20 of 0.293, outperforming five learned recommenders (at most 0.244) but not a previous-day repetition heuristic (0.321). On held-out four-person households, Nash allocation reduces Gini disparity by 42% relative to conflict resolution while improving Recall@20 from 0.180 to 0.197. It comes within 2% of an upper bound on the smoothed Nash optimum, and rescaling one member's utilities changes at most 1.5% of assignments. All recommendations satisfy the encoded dietary rules, while attribution scores correlate with utility loss upon component removal (r = 0.76). In simulation, shared meals reduce pantry use by about one-third, and weekly rotation increases the worst-off member's utility by 38% over the best fixed meal.
label: cs.AI

description: Macroscopic Nuclear Resonance Energy Transfer Mediated by Coherent Magnons. Phonon-mediated nuclear Resonance Energy Transfer (RET) in metal deuterides is severely constrained by inertial rest-mass dilution, lattice fracture limits, and thermal nuclear spin cancellation. Extending the generalized nuclear Dicke model to Ferromagnetic Resonance (FMR) magnons eliminates mass dilution via hyperfine-amplified M1 coupling while unlocking relativistic Dirac M2 coupling via Overhauser spin polarization. We derive a Suhl-clamped FMR scaling law predicting 14.2 MeV (Pd-106) and 11.4 MeV (Ni-58) breakup neutrons, 19.9 MeV alpha particles, and reconciled sub-keV fusion anomalies.
label: nucl-ex

description: Spin-Dependent Transport in One-Dimensional Mercury- and Silver-Mediated DNA Nanowires. Metallo-DNA nanowires serve as a versatile, programmable scaffold for molecular-scale electronics. In this work, we demonstrate that periodic heavy-metal coordination fundamentally reshapes the electronic landscape of DNA, generating dispersive, metal-centered conduction bands rather than isolated localized states. Driven by enhanced inter-layer coupling, where second nearest-neighbor hopping plays a crucial role: the conduction bandwidth can approach 1 eV, more than double that of canonical DNA. These broad bands suggest enhanced robustness of transport against structural fluctuations. As a result of relativistic effects, in these quasi-one-dimensional materials, spin-orbit (SO) coupling enhances band dispersion and governs spin-dependent transport. We predict that although ligand hybridization reduces atomic SO splitting, the effective SO splitting in these nanowires is comparable to the next-nearest-neighbor hopping strength, which results in considerable spin mixing. We find that Hg2+-coordinated nanowire exhibit pronounced spin-flip conductance comparable to spin-conserving conductance across the LUMO manifold. This efficient spin conversion remains robust over extended molecular lengths and is accompanied by a set of highly delocalized unoccupied states with oscillating nodal structures, readily accessible under low-bias transport measurements. In contrast, the Ag+-coordinated nanowires exhibit weak spin-flip scattering that is more than an order of magnitude smaller than spin-preserving transport. This duality establishes the choice of coordination metal as a decisive parameter to govern metal-metal interaction, electron delocalization, and spin-dependent transport. Overall, our findings demonstrate how relativistic effects and quantum confinement intersect in these bio-templated, quasi-one-dimensional molecular conductors.
label: cond-mat.mes-hall

description: SR-ANM: A Square-Root Atomic Norm Minimization Estimator for Noise-Robust Direction-of-Arrival Estimation. This paper proposes a Square-root Atomic Norm Minimization (SR-ANM) estimator for direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation in the single measurement vector (SMV) setting. This new framework, inspired by the Square-root Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (Square-root LASSO), relies on a residual term based on the $L_{2}$-norm rather than the usual squared $L_{2}$-norm so as to obtain an estimator whereby the hyperparameter of the atomic norm in the unconstrained convex optimization problem exhibits robustness to the noise level compared to classical ANM. Experimental verification across a wide signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) range from 0 dB to 40 dB using the the probability of detection and the angular root-mean-squared error (RMSE) confirms the increased noise robustness of the proposed framework compared to ANM.
label: eess.SP
